T1046.name: Network Service Scanning
T1046.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts.
T1046.detection_note: High unique destination port count from a single source IP.

T1110.name: Brute Force
T1110.description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to gain access to accounts when passwords are unknown.
T1110.detection_note: Repeated failed authentication attempts against a service port.

T1078.name: Valid Accounts
T1078.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access.
T1078.detection_note: High volume of authentication failures suggesting credential stuffing.

T1071.004.name: Application Layer Protocol: DNS
T1071.004.description: Adversaries may communicate using the Domain Name System (DNS) application layer protocol to avoid detection.
T1071.004.detection_note: Long DNS queries with high entropy subdomains indicate DNS tunneling.

T1048.003.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol: Exfiltration Over Unencrypted/Obfuscated Non-C2 Protocol
T1048.003.description: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over a symmetric encrypted network protocol other than that of the existing command and control channel.
T1048.003.detection_note: High bytes_out_ratio to external destination suggests data exfiltration.

T1041.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
T1041.description: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over an existing command and control channel.
T1041.detection_note: Large outbound transfer to external IP consistent with C2 exfiltration.

T1071.001.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
T1071.001.description: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols associated with web traffic.
T1071.001.detection_note: Regular low-byte connections over HTTP/HTTPS indicate C2 beaconing.

T1573.name: Encrypted Channel
T1573.description: Adversaries may employ a known encryption algorithm to conceal command and control traffic.
T1573.detection_note: Encrypted protocol to suspicious external endpoint.

T1498.name: Network Denial of Service
T1498.description: Adversaries may perform Network DoS attacks to degrade or block the availability of targeted resources.
T1498.detection_note: Extremely high packet/byte count consistent with flooding or DDoS.

T1105.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
T1105.description: Adversaries may transfer tools or other files from an external system into a compromised environment.
T1105.detection_note: File transfer with notable payload entropy, consistent with tool staging.

T1204.name: User Execution
T1204.description: An adversary may rely upon specific actions by a user in order to gain execution.
T1204.detection_note: Potential user-triggered file execution via web or file transfer.
